findings.reason: The declared set travels from the loader to SkillRegistry through a WeakMap keyed by object identity, and SkillRegistry.addPluginSkill (skill-registry.ts:493) quietly falls back to the running Host API set (HOST_API_CONTEXT_TYPES) when the lookup misses. Identity holds today because validateSkillContribution returns `c` and listSkills/overlay.skills hand back the same objects. The lowering path already makes a copy, though: validateWritingStyle spreads `{...c}`. A future clone between admission and fan-out would give a package that declared an older Host API the newer set with no warning, and that defeats the freeze. Carry the declared set explicitly, or make a missing record a loud error instead of a fallback for loader-admitted entries.

The unit goal says the contribution scope of both skills and subagents is counted against the declared Host API version's ContextType set. The subagent resolver still accepts any explicit `contextTypes` element without checking it against hostApiContextTypesFor(manifest.hostApiVersion). Only a non-array is rejected, and an unknown element silently never matches. Once a release adds a value, a subagent of a package declaring an older version could still delegate in that turn, and that breaks the freeze.
